sources.name: Identifying property and street information
facts: UPRNs identify every addressable location in Great Britain and USRNs identify streets
UPRN and USRN identifiers with associated grid references are open data under the Open Government Licence
Systems that store or publish property and street information must use the identifiers
Several UPRNs can share one grid reference, for example flats in a block
sources.access_guard: Confirm identifiers are genuine using a trusted source; the number and grid reference alone do not prove a unique parcel polygon.
sources.limitation: A UPRN is an addressable-location identifier and may share coordinates with other UPRNs; it is not a title boundary or broadband serviceability record.
sources.access_and_licence: Official GOV.UK standard under Open Government Licence v3.0

sources.name: Access free address data using AddressBase
sources.publisher: Government Digital Service and Central Digital and Data Office
facts: Public-sector users are advised to use AddressBase Core as the source of truth for Great Britain address data
AddressBase products are available to eligible public-sector organisations under the Public Sector Geospatial Agreement
AddressBase Core identifies properties with UPRNs and locates them on a map
Great Britain coverage excludes Northern Ireland
sources.access_guard: Do not assume this project has PSGA eligibility or licensed AddressBase Core access; open products remain the unattended default.
sources.limitation: Authoritative address access does not itself create a legal parcel-to-UPRN relationship or prove broadband availability.
sources.access_and_licence: Official GOV.UK guidance; PSGA entitlement applies to eligible public-sector organisations

sources.name: Government Property Data Standard GovS004-PDS010
sources.publisher: Cabinet Office and Government Property Function
facts: The standard stores UPRN, coordinate reference system and property boundary as separate fields
Property boundary is defined as spatial polygon extent and has an annual review frequency
UPRN and coordinates are updated on change
Initial verification should include verification of geospatial data
sources.access_guard: A complete property record must preserve the UPRN, CRS and boundary as distinct evidence with change control.
sources.limitation: The standard defines a record model and assurance process; it does not supply a national title polygon or broadband dataset.
sources.access_and_licence: Official GOV.UK publication under Open Government Licence v3.0

sources.name: Unique Property Reference Number policy statement
facts: The UPRN is the identifier for every spatial address in Great Britain
It remains consistent through the property lifecycle from planning to demolition
The UPRN number contains no attribution or coordinate information
Other Ordnance Survey attributes or derived data can require separate licensing
sources.access_guard: Treat the UPRN as an opaque identifier; obtain coordinates, status, classification and geometry from separately licensed and versioned sources.
sources.limitation: No location, parcel geometry, property characteristic or broadband status can be derived from the UPRN number itself.
sources.access_and_licence: Official GeoPlace policy; identifier sharing and source-data licensing conditions remain distinct

sources.name: FindMyAddress lifecycle and search limitations
facts: UPRNs can be assigned from the planning stage and are never reallocated
Individual flats within one block have their own UPRNs
The underlying data is created and maintained by local authorities and published through AddressBase
FindMyAddress is limited to personal non-commercial use with a daily search limit
sources.access_guard: Use only for individual manual validation within stated terms; do not automate or extrapolate the service into a bulk production source.
sources.limitation: Several addressable units can occupy one building; a building footprint or shared point cannot be assigned to one UPRN without unit-level evidence.
sources.access_and_licence: Official GeoPlace service; personal non-commercial and daily-search restrictions apply

sources.name: OS Open Linked Identifiers overview
sources.published_or_updated: Official documentation last updated in 2026; reverified 31 July 2026
facts: The product provides authoritative relationships between UPRNs, USRNs and TOIDs
It contains 11 relationship tables with Great Britain coverage
The join tables contain identifiers and version information but no geometry
Confidence values indicate whether current version information is unchanged, potentially changed or changed from the version used to form the relationship
sources.access_guard: Require relationship method, both identifier versions and confidence value; changed-version relationships cannot be silently promoted.
sources.limitation: A relationship table can link identifiers but supplies no polygon and may become invalid after a source-feature version change.
sources.access_and_licence: Official OS OpenData documentation; Open Government Licence and attribution apply

sources.name: Get energy performance of buildings data
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
facts: The service provides bulk domestic, non-domestic and display energy certificate data for England and Wales
Records include certificates registered since 2012 and can include expired or replaced certificates
Bulk CSV downloads and a developer API are offered
A GOV.UK One Login sign-in or account creation is required for bulk downloads
sources.access_guard: The account-gated route is documented but not accessed; certificate date, status and replacement history are mandatory if used later.
sources.limitation: An EPC record is evidence about a certificate and address, not a title boundary, complete premises inventory or broadband serviceability source.
sources.access_and_licence: Official government service; sign-in and service licensing restrictions apply

sources.name: Energy Performance of Buildings Certificates technical notes
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
facts: Statistical processing removes certificates marked cancelled or not for issue
Records with Scottish addresses are removed from the England and Wales statistical dataset
For new dwellings, duplicate records with the same UPRN and first two address lines retain the most recent certificate
The published methodology explicitly treats certificate status and recency as data-quality controls
sources.access_guard: Retain certificate status, lodgement date and deduplication rule; never count all historical certificates as distinct current premises.
sources.limitation: EPC coverage is incomplete for the full property universe and certificate deduplication does not establish parcel identity.
sources.access_and_licence: Official GOV.UK technical notes under Open Government Licence

sources.name: Connected Nations update Spring 2026
sources.published_or_updated: Published 13 May 2026; January 2026 snapshot; reverified 31 July 2026
facts: The report is a January 2026 snapshot of fixed and mobile network availability
Residential coverage headlines and all-premises measures are not interchangeable
Data collected for the report was used to update Ofcom coverage checkers
The fixed broadband archive is listed as a 32.2 MB download
sources.access_guard: Preserve snapshot date, residential-versus-all-premises scope and archive version; report metadata cannot replace byte-level ZIP validation.
sources.limitation: Aggregate coverage and checker updates do not prove an installed or orderable service at a selected parcel.
sources.access_and_licence: Official Ofcom publication and downloadable data; Ofcom terms apply

sources.name: Connected Nations FAQs
facts: Connected Nations is currently published twice a year
Fixed coverage, fixed performance and mobile data are separate downloads
Since July 2024 Ofcom no longer publishes a fixed performance postcode file
Ofcom considers the revised performance data robust to local-authority level but not postcode level
sources.access_guard: Do not infer postcode performance from local-authority aggregates or from older postcode-performance releases.
sources.limitation: Publication cadence and aggregate performance data cannot establish current parcel-level service quality.
sources.access_and_licence: Official Ofcom FAQ and data terms

sources.name: Connected Nations update Spring 2025 historical downloads
sources.published_or_updated: Published 8 May 2025; historical source rechecked 31 July 2026
facts: The Spring 2025 publication used a January 2025 data snapshot
It listed separate postcode and output-area fixed coverage archives
The postcode archive was listed as 25.9 MB and the output-area archive as 8.9 MB
The publication stated its reported coverage used the prior CN2024 methodology
sources.access_guard: Historical files may be used only for versioned comparison; do not mix their schema, epoch or methodology with the corrected January 2026 archive.
sources.limitation: A previous-year postcode file is stale evidence and cannot fill missing current parcel results.
sources.access_and_licence: Official historical Ofcom publication; Ofcom terms apply

sources.name: UK Geospatial Data Standards Register
facts: The register identifies UPRN and USRN as standards for unambiguous and persistent property and street identification
UK GEMINI is the UK profile of ISO 19115 for geospatial metadata
Metadata and identifier standards are complementary rather than substitutes
Current INSPIRE guidance should also be considered when data is within scope
sources.access_guard: Every spatial evidence record must retain identifier, source, epoch, CRS and metadata profile; an identifier alone is not sufficient provenance.
sources.limitation: A standards register governs representation and metadata but supplies neither parcel geometry nor broadband coverage.
sources.access_and_licence: Official GOV.UK standards register under Open Government Licence
